subject: Clarifying Hosted API fit and traffic profile — next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@shopwise.ai>
Cc: Tom Greene <t.greene@shopwise.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Clarifying Hosted API fit and traffic profile — next steps

Hi Asha — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the right evaluation path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

Summary of what I heard on the call:
- Primary use case: post-purchase customer support summarization and FAQ generation for ShopWise mobile/web.
- PII note: support transcripts include names and order IDs; no full-card storage in payloads.
- Initial scope: ~1M monthly requests (mixed short prompts + 50–150 token responses).
- Peak profile: expected spikes tied to promotions, ~120 RPS for 5–10 minute windows.
- Latency requirement: customer-experience target is p95 < 750 ms for reply generation.

What we need from you to recommend the best path and pilot setup:
1) Confirm weekly/monthly QPS and typical burst sizes (can drop a CSV if easier).
2) Which data residency/regulatory limits apply? (Do we need EU-only, or is US ok?)
3) Are you open to starting on Hosted API for the pilot if we can meet the p95 SLA and provide a canary throughput plan?
4) Any procurement constraints that would force Dedicated/Private early (e.g., must be vendor-installed on VPC before signing)?

Next steps I propose:
- You share a simple traffic snapshot and one representative prompt/response pair (we can use it for latency/cost estimates).
- We stand up a 2-week Hosted pilot (verified model variant + rate limit plan) with a small reserved token pool and telemetry access for ShopWise. If traffic profile warrants, we outline Dedicated capacity sizing.

Attachments: I attached a short template to collect traffic details (shopwise_ml_req_template.xlsx) and our Hosted Quickstart PDF.

If that plan sounds reasonable, can you send the traffic snapshot and confirm procurement constraints? Happy to book a 20-minute follow-up next week.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Asha Menon <asha@shopwise.ai>

Cc: Tom Greene <t.greene@shopwise.ai>, procurement@shopwise.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Clarifying Hosted API fit and traffic profile — next steps

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear summary. A few answers inline: 

1) Traffic snapshot: attaching our last 30-day request counts and a CSV with minute-level peaks (shopwise_prod_traffic_snapshot.csv). Typical baseline is ~400 RPS across geographies during business hours; promotions drive short 2–8 minute spikes up to ~150 RPS. Monthly requests ~1.1M.
2) Residency: US-only for now (marketing & legal confirmed). No EU-only requirement.
3) Pilot: We're open to starting on Hosted API for a 2-week pilot, provided you can demonstrate that p95 < 750 ms during a staged spike.
4) Procurement: procurement@shopwise.ai will need a vendor questionnaire and a standard MSA redline. They prefer to review SOC 2 and data processing addenda early.

Also attaching a sample prompt/response pair and the traffic CSV. Let me know if you need tokenized counts; our engineering team can add those.

—Asha
Asha Menon
Head of ML | ShopWise
asha@shopwise.ai
[attachment: shopwise_prod_traffic_snapshot.csv (csv)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Tom Greene <t.greene@shopwise.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Clarifying Hosted API fit and traffic profile — next steps

On Wed, 30 Jun 2027 18:05:00 +0000, Asha Menon wrote:
> Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear summary. A few answers inline: ...

Perfect, thanks for the files — they make sizing straightforward. Quick initial read and recommended pilot path: 

- Hosted pilot is reasonable: start with a verified medium-latency model variant and a staged-load test to validate p95 during spikes. We can provision throttle windows so promotional bursts won’t blow past your cost expectations.
- Given your baseline (~400 RPS) and spikes (~150 RPS), Dedicated isn't immediately required, but we should define an escalation threshold (e.g., sustained >600 RPS for 24 hours) that would trigger a Dedicated sizing convo.
- For the pilot we'll provide:
  * A dedicated API key and scoped telemetry dashboard
  * A suggested rate-limit configuration (baseline RPS + burst tokens)
  * A short smoke test script your engineers can run to simulate spikes
  * SOC 2 + DPA for procurement to review (I attached links in the HubSpot record; procurement contact copied).

Marissa — can you own the pilot setup (billing scope + telemetry access) and drop the proposed rate-limit config? Logan — please prepare a quick suggested stress test script (one-liner curl + python harness) we can share.

Asha — I'll schedule a 20-minute sync for next Tue to align on test window and procurement kickoff.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, procurement@shopwise.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Clarifying Hosted API fit and traffic profile — next steps

Hi Asha — looping in procurement and ops details so we can move quickly.

Planned pilot checklist (high level):
- Pilot length: 2 weeks (configurable)
- Model variant: r-instruct-medium (we'll confirm per your sample prompt)
- Rate limits: initial baseline 450 RPS with burst tokens up to 700 for 5-minute windows; will instrument throttling policies that return 429 with Retry-After when exceeded.
- Telemetry: read-only dashboard + request-level traces for your engineers.
- Cost & billing: temporary pilot credits applied to baseline usage; overage billing flagged and paused until procurement approves.
- Security: SOC 2 report and DPA link will be shared; if you need hosted VPC for the pilot please flag now (likely adds lead time).

Action items: 
- Asha/procurement: confirm SOC2/DPA acceptance path and any procurement SLAs (timeline).
- Tom: validate that the test prompt in the sample is representative.
- Logan: share the stress test script (cc'd).
- Rafael: please send the HubSpot link and the DocuSign template for the pilot agreement.

I'll stand up the pilot once we have procurement signoff and your final go for the test window.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
